description:
login.advancelogin_advanceAdvance the sign-in on the current tab: account choice, consent, filling the saved username and password, entering a one-time code, and checking the result.

Give `tab`, the sign-in `status` you observe, and the field or button references the current step needs. The credential service takes the account from your sign-in context, obtains the user's consent and fills the fields without revealing them. Your sign-in context holds the account from the `account_hint` that started or followed up your work, or the one Muse chose since. The result gives the status, the account's label, anything unresolved and the page after the fill when available. Use that page to choose your next step; observe only when the view you need is missing or has changed. A result that stops short of a sign-in names the sign-in page's site.

The call waits for sign-in approval or secure entry and resumes when that input arrives. If the user declines, it asks Muse how to proceed and returns the decline with Muse's answer; read that answer before taking another step. When consent is granted and the page redrew meanwhile, it finds the same fields and provider control on the page as it is then, so the user is not asked twice; a field the site cleared, such as after a CAPTCHA, is filled again under the same approval. After a site rejected a sign-in, whether to try again is your decision; say what the page shows in `previous_attempt`. On a code step, the call reads the one-time code from the user's mail or asks Muse for it, and waits. Once the user approves it, the service types it into `code_fields` and clicks `code_submit_button`, and the result returns the page after the entry, never the code. When the user declines, the code expired or Muse answers without one, nothing is entered and the result says so. The call cannot switch accounts, resend a code or get around a lockout. A purchase whose outcome is still unknown does not hold the sign-in. If the page changes, call `login.advance` again with your assessment of the new observation it returns.

After `wait_interrupted`, read the new message in your conversation before continuing. For `credential_input_mismatch`, use the reported provider and field types to reassess the page or ask Muse for the missing choice. Treat `credentials_updated` or a runtime `credential_update` as new information under your current assignment, then reassess with `login.advance` if sign-in is still needed.

status.description: The sign-in step the current page shows. A user_control page can show a number or code that the user matches or types on their own device to approve. They can approve only once they are told it, so the summary of your report gives it first, exactly as the page shows it.

username_field.description: The reference of the visible, editable username, email or phone field for the current sign-in step, from controls; null when absent, read-only or disabled, including a read-only account identifier on a password-only step.

password_field.description: The reference of the visible, editable password field for the current sign-in step, from controls; null when absent, read-only or disabled.

google_button.description: The reference of the visible Google sign-in control, whatever element it is, such as a button, a link or a framed button; null when the page shows none.

apple_button.description: The reference of the visible Apple sign-in control, whatever element it is, such as a button, a link or a framed button; null when the page shows none.

amazon_button.description: The reference of the visible Amazon sign-in control, whatever element it is, such as a button, a link or a framed button; null when the page shows none.

code_fields.description: On a code step, the references of the boxes that take the one-time code, from controls, in reading order: one box, or one per character when the site splits the code; null on every other step.

code_submit_button.description: On a code step, the reference of the button that submits the code, such as Verify, from the page; null when the page submits the code by itself or on every other step.

code_sent_to.description: On a code step, where the page says it sent the code, as the page shows it, such as a masked email address or the last digits of a phone number; null when the page does not say.

previous_attempt.description: What the page shows about an earlier sign-in attempt: rejected when it shows one failed, such as a wrong password message, none when it shows no earlier attempt, unknown otherwise.
